findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: There was a dented can of beets stored on a rack with other canned goods. The PIC pulled the can from the shelf to correct the violation. Ensure that canned goods are free of any dents along the seams and body of the can to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There was a container of tomato bisque soup and chili stored inside of the main walk in cooler that exceeded the seven day holding timeframe. The items were date marked July 26, 2026 and July 27, 2026. Discussed with the PIC and the soups were discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that temperature/time control (TCS) foods are never held past their seven day date marking.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: The two door prep cooler along the cook line was observed with a broken door handle. The PIC mentioned that the handle broke a few weeks prior to the inspection. Ensure that the handle is repaired and is in good condition.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following areas are in need of cleaning:
- the top surface of the drawer cooler was observed with accumulated grease and food debris
- the bottom shelf of the drawer cooler was observed with accumulated spilled liquids and food debris

The PIC instructed an employee to clean the surfaces during the visit. Ensure that non food contact surfaces of pieces of equipment are cleaned at a frequency to prevent accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment:
The following canned food items were observed to have dents around their seams:
1. Mandarin oranges
2. Whole peeled potatoes x2

CORRECTED - The person-in-charged (PIC) was informed and the dented cans were removed from the shelf. Ensure dented cans are removed from the shelf due to potential contaminants from exposure.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [PF]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following nonfood-contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:
1. Bottom of the 3-door cooler at the back storage area has soil accumulation.
2. Shelf for storing clean pots at the walk way has dust accumulation.
3. Shelf for storing clean plate at the salad bar has dust accumulation.

The PIC was informed. Ensure the surfaces mentioned above are cleaned to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: A ground beef roll was observed thawing in a sink with plugged water. The PIC unplugged the sink and provided running water to correct the violation. If using the running water method for thawing, be sure to never plug sink so that water is never at a stand still and continuously flowing.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The baffles of the hood system (above the fryers) were observed heavily accumulated with grease debris. Discussed and shown to PIC. The facility has CFB Steam Power for servicing the hood system, however, the baffles are able to be cleaned manually in a ware-washing sink or dish machine. Ensure that hood baffles are cleaned as often as necessary to avoid grease buildup.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: A pot of Chili that was being held on the frontline warmer was probed between 123F -126F. The PIC mentioned that the chili was recently placed on the warmer. The Chili was reheated in the steamer to at least 165F to correct the violation. Be sure that hot held foods are maineded at 135F or above to ensure proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Stainless steel lids and food debris were observed at the bottom of the drawer coolers. Discussed and shown to PIC. The surface was cleaned during the inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent buildup.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: The faucet of the triple sink was observed leaking water into the basin of the sink. Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure that faucets are maintained in good repair and are in leak free condition.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed a container of diced tomatoes to be out of date in the walk in cooler. The tomatoes were dated 4/8/2024. PIC pulled tomatoes from cooler. Ensure that TCS foods that are held in house longer than 24 hours are discarded if not used within 7 days.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Facility could not locate a temperature measuring device for their dish machine. PIC mentioned that they were new to the facility and is unaware of where the device might be located. PIC made a store run and was able to purchase temperature thermo labels to properly measure the dish machine’s sanitizing temperature. 

4-302.13: (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessib  le for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed several used mop heads stored on the floor and inside of the mop basin. PIC repositioned mop heads and placed others in the laundry bin. Ensure that mop heads are stored in a manner that allows for them to air dry properly. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Hand washing sink did not have soap at time of inspection.  Discussed with PIC, who stated he would have maintenance put a new soap in.  Ensure hand sinks are properly supplied during all hours of operation.

6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Sanitizer buckets and 3 part sink had a concentration of 100 ppm (q) at time of inspection.  After replacing the sanitizer bag, the concentration was at 300 ppm.  Check sanitizer concentration regularly to ensure the sanitizer is at the correct concentration.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Multiple out of date containers were observed in the walk-in cooler.  Discussed with PIC and employees, and all containers were pulled and discarded.  Ensure all items are checked regularly and out of date items are discarded.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The top of the knife holder was observed to contain dust and food debris on the top.  Discussed with PIC.  Ensure the tops of the knife holders are cleaned regularly.

4-601.11: (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Areas in need of re-caulking:
-3 part sink
-hand sinks
Ensure sinks are caulked to create a smooth and easily cleanable surface.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority violations were observed for food not being in sound condition, cross contamination, sanitization, cold holding, cooling, and chemical storage. See violations 13, 15, 16, 20, 22, & 28 for details. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at re-inspection next month.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing sign was not posted at the handwashing sink in the back prep area adjacent to the dish area. Handwashing sign was provided to be posted.
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.citation_text:
3-101.11 Container labeled as plain gravy was observed intermixed with containers of sausage gravy in the bar walk-in cooler. Container with plain gravy had two date marks, with one as 4/25 and the other as 5/11. Other containers of sausage gravy in the walk-in were prepared the day prior on 5/11 and not properly cooled (see #20 for details). The plain gravy had an internal temperature of 36F and had a spoiled smell. Plain gravy was discarded during inspection. 
Food shall be safe, unadulterated, and honestly presented as specified under 3-601.12.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Aluminum pans of thawing lasagna mix were observed on the top shelf in the walk-in cooler. Condensation was dripping from the bottom of pans down on top of a bowl of chicken salad and trays with bacon covered by parchment paper. Proper storage of thawing products to avoid potential cross contamination was discussed. Products were rearranged to allow for thawing without potential cross contamination.
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Multiple spray bottles labeled as sanitizer (Shurguard and Kay Quat II) were observed with concentrations of 0ppm and 100ppm. A freshly prepared sani-bucket was also observed with a concentration of 0ppm quat. Another fresh solution was prepared for the sani-bucket and observed at 200ppm. Fresh solutions in spray bottles were initially observed at 0ppm. Quat solution was not consistently dispensing at 200ppm. Store manager ran the dispenser for several seconds at which time the concentration was then observed at 200ppm. Restaurant manager was advised to allow the dispenser to run for several seconds prior to filling bottles and buckets. Allow foam to settle before using test strips to check the concentration of liquid. Verify proper concentration of quat solutions prior to use. Also, ensure quat solitons in spray bottles are checked with test strips frequently to verify proper concentration and fresh solutions are provided as needed.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text:
3-501.14 Sausage gravy cooked the day prior on 5/11 did not cool properly. Gravy was observed in 22qt containers in the walk-in coolers (one in the main walk-in and three in the bar walk-in). Condensation was on the inner surface of lids, indicating product was placed in the coolers and covered during the cooling process. Surface temperatures were at 46F-49F, while internal temperatures were observed at 55F, 59.5F, and 60.5F. Gravy was prepared between 10am-12pm the day prior. Employee helping with prep stated the blast chiller was not used, and product was placed directly in walk-in coolers. All gravy was discarded during inspection. Proper cooling was discussed, and educational handout was provided for management to re-educate staff.
Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. 
Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Two boxes of bacon were observed on the back prep table. An open box with partially used product had surface temperatures at 45F-49F. Trays of bacon were observed with surface temperatures of 55F-60F. All bacon was moved to the walk-in cooler to chill and store product until proper attention could be given for prep/cooking. Best practices were discussed. Ensure only the amount of needed product is removed for prep from coolers. Promptly use TCS foods and/or place them back in cold holding when interruptions in tasks occur to limit temperature abuse. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Spray bottle without a label was observed at front service area. Product was confirmed to be quat sanitizer below proper concentration. Corrective actions were taken to provide sanitizer at proper concentration and label the bottle as to the contents.
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-201.11 Spray bottles of sanitizer and oven cleaner were improperly stored. Sanitizer was observed hanging on a cart next to and above salt and other seasonings. Oven cleaner was on a lower shelf intermixed with single service items. Bottles were relocated to allow for proper storage.
Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they cannot contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, single service and single use articles by separating toxic materials by spacing or partitioning and locating toxic materials in an area that is not above food, equipment, utensils, linens, single service and single use articles.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-803.11 Soiled wiping cloths were observed on a back table next to a coffee maker and on a storage shelf next to clean equipment. Ensure soiled wiping cloths are properly stored after use and not left laying around the prep and storage areas.
Soiled linens shall be kept in clean, nonabsorbent receptacles or clean, washable laundry bags and stored and transported to prevent contamination of food, clean equipment, clean utensils, and single-service and single-use articles. Store soiled wiping cloths in the storage container when no longer needed.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.13 Facility has a heat sanitizing dish machine. An irreversible registering temperature indicator was not available for checking the surface temperature at the dishes during a ware washing cycle. Options for dish machine temperature test strips and maximum registering thermometers were discussed.
In hot water mechanical warewashing operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature. Surface temperature at dishes upon completion of final rinse must be at least 160F for proper heat sanitization.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed mold on the fan in the walk in cooler. This could contaminate food in the cooler if food is cooling or left uncovered. Ensure the fan is cleaned frequently to prevent mold and dust accumulation. The fan was cleaned during the inspection. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed multiple foods in the prep cooler and both walk in coolers with foods that exceeded the 7 day date marking. All foods that exceeded the 7 day date marking (foods prepared on 6-29 and prior) were discarded to correct the violation. Ensure foods are discarded when the 7 day date marking is exceeded. 

3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Observed dozens of drain flies in the dish area and multiple drain flies in the food prep area. Eliminate drain flies from the establishment. The manager stated she has a spray called Zeevo that she will use on walls and equipment. She stated she will not use it on food contact surfaces. Additionally, she will contact Plunkett’s Pest Control for further solutions.  

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed a mop across from the walk in cooler to not be stored in a position that allows it to air dry. The mop was stored inside the mop bucket. Wet mops not stored properly can attract drain flies. Ensure mops are stored in a position that allows them to air dry properly. The mop was moved in a correct position during the inspection. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: Observed grits in a prep cooler dated 12-23. This exceeds the 7 day date marking criteria. The grits were discarded to correct the violation. Ensure foods are discarded when the 7 day date marking is exceeded. 
(A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Observed the quat sani bucket concentration to be 0ppm. Ensure the concentration of quat is maintained between 200ppm and 400ppm. The sani bucket was replaced during the inspection. 
Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: Observed milk in the walk in cooler to not be date marked. Ensure milk is properly date marked. Milk date marked during the inspection. 
(A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: Observed ice wands to be placed on the shelf in the walk in freezer. Ice wands are considered a food contact surface. The shelf is not considered a clean and sanitized surface. Ensure the ice wands are placed in a clean and sanitized container to avoid contamination of the ice wands. The ice wands were placed in a clean container during the inspection.
(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.
